key_insight: A combined CEL simulation and ANN framework can accurately predict weld temperature, axial force, and defect formation in friction stir welding of HDPE, enabling rapid identification of defect-free process windows.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical process maps and design guidance for optimizing thermoplastic FSW by balancing rotation speed, travel speed, and preheating to improve joint quality and force stability.
method: 3D coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE FSW
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and axial-force histories
Parameter sweep over rotational speed, welding speed, and bottom preheating to map defects vs. safe windows
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong predictive performance with R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL results agreed well with experimental observations of voids, thermal response, and forces.
watch_item: The trained models and process maps are likely specific to the tested HDPE setup and parameter range, so transfer to other polymers, tool geometries, or thicknesses may require retraining and revalidation.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
